def-ip-feature-estimability-through-adjo:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space. Let $K:X\to H$ be bounded and linear, let $\epsilon>0$, and let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. For each $x\in X$ define $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. A continuous linear feature is a map $\phi\in X^*$, where $X^*$ is the continuous dual of $X$. By the Riesz representation theorem there is a unique $h_\phi\in X$ with $\phi(x)=\langle x,h_\phi\rangle_X$ for every $x\in X$. The feature is **exactly linearly estimable by one probe** if some $\Phi\in H$ makes the statistic $Y_x(\Phi)$ unbiased for $\phi(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Writing $R(K^*)=\{K^*\Phi:\Phi\in H\}$ for the adjoint range, this holds exactly when $h_\phi\in R(K^*)$. Every such probe has variance $\epsilon^2\|\Phi\|_H^2$. This definition concerns one-probe unbiased linear estimators; it does not identify membership in $\overline{R(K^*)}$ with exact estimability.
thm-ip-isonormal-gaussian-posterior-law:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ and $H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces with supplied finite or countable complete orthonormal bases $(v_j)$ and $(e_n)$. Let $K:X\to H$ be bounded and linear, let $\epsilon>0$, and let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian random element with mean $m_0\in X$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$. Let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$, independent of $U$, and observe the random field
$$Y(g)=\langle KU,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g),\qquad g\in H,$$
on $\mathbb R^H$ with its cylinder sigma-algebra $\mathcal C_H$; write $P_Y$ for the law of this field. Write $S=C_0^{1/2}$,
$$B=SK^*KS,\qquad R=(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1},\qquad C_{\rm post}=\epsilon^2SRS,$$
and for $h\in X$ put
$$\Phi_h=KSRSh.$$
For $y\in\mathbb R^H$, set
$$b_j(y)=\langle m_0,v_j\rangle_X+y(\Phi_{v_j})-\langle Km_0,\Phi_{v_j}\rangle_H.$$
If $\sum_j b_j(y)^2<\infty$, define $M_y=\sum_jb_j(y)v_j$; otherwise define $M_y=m_0$. In finite dimension these sums terminate, and an empty basis is allowed for the zero space.

There is a data-indexed probability kernel $\Pi_y$ on $X$ that is a regular conditional law of $U$ given the field $Y$, and for every $y$ it is the Borel Gaussian law with mean $M_y$ and covariance $C_{\rm post}$. In particular, for every fixed $h\in X$ and every Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\Pi_y\{u:\langle u,h\rangle_X\in A\}=N\!\left(\langle M_y,h\rangle_X,\langle C_{\rm post}h,h\rangle_X\right)(A).$$
For each fixed $h$, for $P_Y$-almost every $y$,
$$\langle M_y,h\rangle_X=\langle m_0,h\rangle_X+y(\Phi_h)-\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H.$$
The exceptional null set in this identity may depend on $h$; no simultaneous identity for every $h$ on one sample set is asserted. Here $N(a,\sigma^2)$ denotes the scalar normal law of mean $a$ and variance $\sigma^2$, including the zero-variance point mass.
alg-ip-gaussian-map-feature-test:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces, let $K:X\to H$ be bounded, and let $\epsilon>0$. Let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $m_0$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. For parameter $x\in X$, the observation field is $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. Fix a feature vector $h\in X$. Let
$$S=C_0^{1/2},\qquad B=SK^*KS,\qquad R=(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1},\qquad \Phi_h=KSRSh,$$
and define the raw threshold
$$c_h=\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H-\langle m_0,h\rangle_X.$$
Given a white-noise observation field $y\in\mathbb R^H$, the **Gaussian MAP feature test** returns $1$ exactly when $y(\Phi_h)>c_h$ and returns $0$ otherwise. This strict raw comparison defines the procedure for every field input $y$.

For the posterior kernel $\Pi_y$ with mean $M_y$ supplied by the Gaussian posterior-law theorem, the scalar feature marginal has mode $\langle M_y,h\rangle_X$ for every $y$, with the support point serving as the mode for a zero-variance marginal. For each fixed $h$, under that theorem's prior-predictive observation law $P_Y$, the raw rule agrees for $P_Y$-almost every $y$ with the test that returns $1$ exactly when this posterior marginal mode is positive. The exceptional null set may depend on $h$; no simultaneous equivalence for all features on one sample set is asserted.

If $h=0$, then $\Phi_h=0$ and $c_h=0$. Under every sampling law, $Y_x(0)=0$ almost surely, so the raw test returns $0$ almost surely for observations; the same holds under $P_Y$.
thm-ip-map-test-level-and-power:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces, $K:X\to H$ bounded and linear, $\epsilon>0$, and let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $m_0$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. Fix $h\in X$, define $S=C_0^{1/2}$, $B=SK^*KS$, $R=(B+\epsilon^2I)^{-1}$, $\Phi_h=KSRSh$, and $c_h=\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H-\langle m_0,h\rangle_X$. Let $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$ and let the raw MAP test reject exactly when $Y_x(\Phi_h)>c_h$. Define $G(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-s^2/2}\,ds$, the standard normal cumulative distribution function. For every $x\in X$ its rejection probability is
$$\mathbb P_x\{Y_x(\Phi_h)>c_h\}=\begin{cases}G\!\left(\dfrac{\langle x,K^*\Phi_h\rangle_X-c_h}{\epsilon\|\Phi_h\|_H}\right),&\Phi_h\ne0,\\[6pt]\mathbf1\{0>c_h\},&\Phi_h=0.\end{cases}$$

For a further real Hilbert space $V$ continuously and injectively embedded in $X$ by $i:V\to X$, define the residual functional $r_\Phi\in V^*$, where $V^*$ is the continuous dual of $V$, by
$$r_\Phi(v)=\langle Ki(v),\Phi\rangle_H-\langle i(v),h\rangle_X,\qquad \|r_\Phi\|_{V^*}=\sup_{\|v\|_V\le1}|r_\Phi(v)|.$$
For $0<\alpha<1$ let $z_{1-\alpha}$ satisfy $G(z_{1-\alpha})=1-\alpha$. If $\Phi\ne0$, the calibrated probe test rejects exactly when
$$Y_x(\Phi)>\epsilon\|\Phi\|_H z_{1-\alpha}+\|r_\Phi\|_{V^*}.$$
Its rejection probability at every $x\in X$ is the same displayed Gaussian-tail formula with $\Phi$ in place of $\Phi_h$ and calibrated threshold in place of $c_h$. If $x=i(v)$ satisfies $\|v\|_V\le1$ and $\langle x,h\rangle_X\le0$, this test has rejection probability at most $\alpha$. For $\Phi=0$ it never rejects and has level zero.

As an additional weighted-regularization identity, assume Countable Choice and suppose that $C_0K^*K=K^*KC_0$. Let $J$ be the real partial isometry in the polar decomposition $K=J(K^*K)^{1/2}$. Let $\mathcal D=\{C_0^{1/2}x:x\in X\}$, and define $C_0^{-1/2}$ as the inverse of $C_0^{1/2}$ on $\mathcal D$. On $\Psi\in H$, set
$$J_h(\Psi)=\|K^*\Psi-h\|_X^2+\epsilon^2\|C_0^{-1/2}J^*\Psi\|_X^2$$
when $J^*\Psi\in\mathcal D$, and set $J_h(\Psi)=+\infty$ otherwise. Then $\Phi_h$ is a minimizer of $J_h$, and
$$K^*\Phi_h=B(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1}h.$$
thm-ip-unrestricted-map-test-can-have-le:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces, $K:X\to H$ bounded and linear, $\epsilon>0$, and let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $m_0$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. Put $S=C_0^{1/2}$, $B=SK^*KS$, $R=(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1}$. For a feature vector $h\in X$, define $\Phi_h=KSRSh$, $c_h=\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H-\langle m_0,h\rangle_X$, and the raw test $\delta_h=\mathbf1\{Y_x(\Phi_h)>c_h\}$, where $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. Suppose $C_0K^*K=K^*KC_0$, $h\ne0$, and $Bh$ is not a scalar multiple of $h$. Then the unrestricted null set $H_0=\{x\in X:\langle x,h\rangle_X\le0\}$ satisfies
$$\sup_{x\in H_0}\mathbb P_x\{\delta_h=1\}=1.$$
The supremum need not be attained at any finite parameter value.
